questions.q: When does a real merge conflict actually happen?
options: When two branches change the same lines of the same file in different ways, and Git can't tell which version you want
Any time you run git merge, regardless of what changed
Only when merging main into itself
Whenever two different files are edited by two different people
questions.explain: Git auto-merges non-overlapping changes just fine; a conflict only happens on genuinely overlapping edits to the same lines.

questions.q: In a real conflict block, what does the section between <<<<<<< HEAD and ======= represent?
options: Your current branch's version of that content
The incoming branch's version of that content
A syntax error Git wants you to delete entirely
A comment that Git will strip out automatically
questions.explain: <<<<<<< HEAD marks the start of your current branch's version; the block after ======= is the incoming branch's version.

questions.q: What are the three real choices for resolving a conflict, according to this lesson?
options: Pick one side entirely, combine both, or write something new
Delete the file, restart the branch, or ignore the conflict
Always automatically accept the incoming branch's version
Always automatically accept your own branch's version
questions.explain: You genuinely decide: keep one side, merge the intent of both, or realize neither original version was correct and write a new one.

questions.q: After manually editing a file to resolve a conflict during a merge, what finishes the process?
options: git add <file>, then git commit
Simply saving the file is enough — no further Git commands needed
git push immediately, with no add or commit
Deleting the .git folder and starting over
questions.explain: Once the marker lines are removed and the file is correct, git add stages the resolution and git commit finishes the merge.

questions.q: What does Git refuse to let you do until every conflict marker is removed from every affected file?
options: Commit
Open the file in a text editor
Run git status
Create a new unrelated branch
questions.explain: git status will keep reporting unresolved conflicts, and Git won't let the commit (or rebase --continue) complete until they're all cleared.
